identity.title: A radio census of the massive stellar cluster Westerlund 1

paper_type_evidence.quote: Observations were carried out in 2015 and 2016 with the Australia telescope compact array (ATCA) at 5.5 and 9$\,$GHz using multiple configurations
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA/2013.1.00897.S.

evidence.quote: It has a current age estimate of 5$\,$Myr and a distance estimate of 5$\,$kpc.

question.value: Measure radio fluxes, spectral indices and mass-loss rates of massive stars in Westerlund 1 with ATCA (compared with earlier ALMA 100 GHz data) and characterise the diffuse cluster emission

evidence.quote: We aim to study the radio emission from Westerlund 1, in order to measure radio fluxes from the population of massive stars, and determine mass-loss rates and spectral indices where possible.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA/2013.1.00897.S.

provided.value: New 5.5 and 9 GHz continuum observations in four configurations (750C, 1.5A, 1.5B, 6A); the main dataset of the paper

evidence.quote: The data were collected over two spectral windows, with central frequencies 5.5$\,$GHz, and 9$\,$GHz, and a bandwidth of 2$\,$GHz for each band.

provided.value: Previously published millimetre fluxes and limits, re-tapered to match ATCA uv range for spectral indices and clumping ratios

evidence.quote: The spectral indices of all prior known sources were calculated by comparing source fluxes at three frequencies; 5.5$\,$GHz, 9$\,$GHz and 100$\,$GHz.

method.value: MIRIAD calibration, SERPent flagging, CASA self-cal and multiscale MFS tclean

evidence.quote: After calibration, data were concatenated in several forms, discussed in detail below
the cell size was set to 0.3$\times$0.3$\,$arcseconds

method.value: SEAC floodfill source extraction with watershed segmentation (NOISE and GAUSS) for core/total components

evidence.quote: These were set at 5$\sigma$ for the seed threshold and 3$\sigma$ for the flood threshold.

key_parameters.value: seed 5 sigma, flood 3 sigma, local rms from noise map

evidence.quote: The value of $\sigma$ is the rms value of the local spatial region.

validation.value: Visual inspection and comparison with Do10 8.6 GHz fluxes

evidence.quote: this required a thorough visual inspection of the SEAC results, for all segmentation options, on each dataset

method.value: Taper ATCA and ALMA data to common uv range, measure core fluxes with matched source sizes

evidence.quote: tapering was applied to datasets of ATCA and ALMA observations, so that only equivalent u-v ranges were considered

method.value: Wright & Barlow (1975) formula from flux; clumping ratio from ratio of Mdot*fcl^0.5 at radio vs ALMA assuming constant Mdot

evidence.quote: The Wright and Barlow equation was applied to determine radio mass-loss rates

assumptions.value: Distance 5 kpc; Te = 0.5 Teff for hot stars, 10,000 K for cool stars; mu 1.4/2.0/4/4.7 by type; spherical smooth thermal wind

evidence.quote: The distance, $D$, was assumed to be 5$\,$kpc, as justified in the Introduction.

validation.value: Comparison with mm and optical literature mass-loss rates

evidence.quote: Our value for WR S, $\dot{M}f_{cl}^{\frac{1}{2}}$ 6.3$\,\pm\,$1.2$\,\times\,$10$^{-6}$ $M_{\odot}$$\,$yr$^{-1}$, is larger than determined by previous modelling of this object
Data reduction and calibration was carried out with the use of MIRIAD$\,$(cite: Miriad)
This involved the use of CASA$\,$(cite: Casa), where the functions GAINCAL and APPLYCAL were carried out
analysis was carried out on the datasets using SEAC[^3], a source extraction software tool

used_for.value: image alignment and Gaussian size fitting

evidence.quote: Measurements of the spatial extents were made using JMFIT in AIPS to determine a Gaussian fit for the source.
additional flagging of data carried out in astronomical image processing software (AIPS) with the use of scripted e-MERLIN RFI mitigation pipeline
These radio observations led to 30 radio detections of known stellar sources in Westerlund 1
with a value of $\alpha$ = 0.68$\,\pm\,$0.02
with a mean mass-loss rate over the total ensemble calculated to be 4.61 $\times$ 10$^{-5}$ M$_{\odot}$$\,$yr$^{-1}$
gave a value of 29$\,$M$_{\odot}$, (assuming a general plasma temperature of 10kK)

findings_qualitative.value: Most WRs have spectral indices consistent with thermal winds; the OB supergiant limits are negative, giving 3 new binary candidates

evidence.quote: These detections have led to evidence for 3 new OB supergiant binary candidates, inferred from derived spectral index limits.

claims.hypothesis: Do the massive stars in Wd1 show radio emission, and what is its nature?
claims.experiment: ATCA 5.5/9 GHz imaging, SEAC extraction, radio-mm spectral indices
claims.result: 30 stellar detections; most WRs thermal; WR B negative index
claims.finding: Many stars have thermal wind emission, with a few non-thermal binary candidates

evidence.quote: 30 stars were detected in the radio from the fully concatenated dataset

claims.hypothesis: Is wind clumping decreasing outward in WRs?
claims.experiment: Compare Mdot*fcl^0.5 from tapered ATCA with ALMA
claims.result: Ratios below 1 for most of 7 WRs; WR D 1.34
claims.finding: Generally supports decreasing clumping with radius, with exceptions

evidence.quote: in general support the belief that in stellar winds, clumping should decrease within the wind as a function of radial distance from the star.

limitations_admitted.value: Diffuse emission may be misattributed to stars; errors are potentially underestimates

evidence.quote: Errors quoted in this paper are therefore potentially underestimates of the true uncertainty on these values

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA data are not reprocessed here; relies on Fenech 2018 values
Core/total flux separation depends on tuned segmentation parameters
Distance 5 kpc vs Gaia 3 kpc affects mass-loss rates (D^1.5)
Binary inference from index limits relies on non-detections in mm
